elements.element: Customer may assign to an affiliate without consent.
elements.evidence: Rendered Art. XXIV(c): "except that Licensee may assign without consent to an Affiliate or to a successor in a merger, acquisition or sale of substantially all assets"; "AFFILIATE" is a defined term in Section 1.1, so the carve-out is operative and not dependent on an undefined trigger.

elements.element: Customer may assign to a successor in a merger, acquisition, or sale of substantially all assets without consent.
elements.evidence: Same inserted exception expressly names "a successor in a merger, acquisition or sale of substantially all assets" and is consent-free ("may assign without consent").

elements.element: Vendor may not assign without Customer's consent.
elements.evidence: New sentence: "Licensor may not assign this Agreement without Licensee's prior written consent" — a direct, unconditional consent requirement on the Vendor side, which did not exist in the original one-way clause.

elements.element: Customer's consent to Vendor assignment is not to be unreasonably withheld.
elements.evidence: "...without Licensee's prior written consent, which shall not be unreasonably withheld" — the reasonableness standard attaches to the Licensor-assignment consent.

elements.element: Vendor may never assign to a Customer competitor.
elements.evidence: "...and may not assign to a competitor of Licensee" — an absolute bar, not qualified by the reasonableness proviso (it is a separate conjunctive prohibition).

elements.element: Customer's change of control gives Vendor no termination right.
elements.evidence: Art. XX(a) as rendered: "A Change of Control ... shall not terminate this Agreement or any of Licensee's rights or licenses hereunder and shall give Licensor no right to terminate this Agreement." The automatic-termination trigger, the Licensor-consent condition and the deemed-reasonable-refusal language are all gone; the "CHANGE OF CONTROL" definition lead-in is retained so the defined term still resolves.

elements.element: Both parties may assign to a successor.
elements.evidence: The redline gives Licensee a consent-free successor right but subjects Licensor to a flat "may not assign this Agreement without Licensee's prior written consent" with no successor carve-out, so the right is not mutual.

elements.element: A successor assignment requires written notice.
elements.evidence: No notice mechanic appears anywhere in the rendered clause; the Licensee carve-out is silent as to notifying Licensor.
The retained/inserted Licensee affiliate exception is a no-consent, non-successor exception, which under the ASSIGN fallback rule defeats "Other assignments require consent."

elements.element: Consent to other assignments is not to be unreasonably withheld.
elements.evidence: The reasonableness standard is attached only to Licensee's consent to a Licensor assignment; the retained Licensee-side requirement ("without Licensor's prior written consent") remains an unqualified, discretionary consent.

reasons: Position-complete at the preferred level: all six preferred elements are met in operative language (consent-free Affiliate/M&A successor carve-out for Licensee; Licensor assignment subject to Licensee's consent not unreasonably withheld; absolute bar on assignment to a Licensee competitor; express statement that a Change of Control neither terminates the Agreement/licences nor gives Licensor a termination right).

The fallback checklist is not satisfied (no mutual successor right, no written-notice mechanic, a retained no-consent affiliate exception, and no reasonableness standard on Licensee-side consent) — but that is immaterial because the preferred level is complete.

Minimality fails on one deletion outside the chosen elements: the redline strikes the Art. XXIV(c) sentence "For purposes of this Agreement, any Change of Control (as defined in Section 13.4(a)) shall be governed by the provisions of the section entitled Change Of Control and not the provisions of this Section." No selected element requires its removal, and it was Customer-favourable — it kept a Change of Control outside the assignment-consent prohibition. Repair: restore that sentence verbatim (or, if the drafter believes the 13.4(a) cross-reference is stale, restore it with the correct section reference) so the edit changes only the assignment carve-outs, the Licensor-assignment restriction and the Art. XX(a) termination trigger.

Practical consequence of that same deletion (flagged for repair, not scored as an intent failure): with the routing sentence gone, a Change of Control that is broader than a "merger, acquisition or sale of substantially all assets" (e.g. a >50% stock transfer under the retained CHANGE OF CONTROL definition) could be argued to fall under the retained Licensee assignment prohibition. Restoring the sentence closes that gap.

Intent is otherwise preserved: the CHANGE OF CONTROL definition lead-in and Art. XX(b) survive, the Art. XX heading still has work to do, the "void and of no effect" sentence and the successors-and-permitted-assigns tail are retained, and no defined term or cross-reference is left dangling. The Article XXII right of first refusal is correctly left to the ROFR/MFN rule and is not double-flagged here.
